title: Most spread, lost classes
hook: Can a useful-looking projection erase the distinction?

knows: Small arithmetic and the prerequisites listed below.
doesNotKnow: retaining most geometric variance need not retain the direction separating labels. Distinct from later PCA compression: the causal witness is loss of class information despite high retained variance.

misconception: retaining most geometric variance need not retain the direction separating labels. Distinct from later PCA compression: the causal witness is loss of class information despite high retained variance.
objective: retaining most geometric variance need not retain the direction separating labels. Distinct from later PCA compression: the causal witness is loss of class information despite high retained variance.

claims.text: Population covariance is computed from four symmetric points. Base covariance diag(9,1) gives x-axis retention90%, overlapping opposite y-sign labels after projection. Scaling y to±4 gives diag(9,16), y retention64% and separate classes. Relabelling base points by x changes no covariance but removes projected class overlap. Original hollow and projected filled circle/square shapes encode the two labels.

claims.text: The retained projection keeps the x direction and 90% of variance, yet opposite classes overlap. PCA uses the geometry, not the labels. Changing labels alone leaves its axis unchanged; changing coordinate scale can change that axis. These are four constructed points, not a test of real-model accuracy.
